12 - types and variants of chess.grand chess: a large-board variant of chess that uses a 10x10 board and introduces additional pieces and expanded rules, offering new strategic possibilities compared to traditional chess
12 - types and variants of chess.sittuyin: a traditional chess variant played in myanmar on a 64-square board with unique pieces and rules distinct from standard chess
12 - types and variants of chess.tamerlane chess: a historical chess variant played on a 10x10 board with extra pieces and unique rules, inspired by the historical conqueror timur

13 - chess terms.chessboard: a square board with a grid of 64 alternating light and dark colored squares arranged in an 8x8 pattern, used for playing the game of chess
13 - chess terms.king: a chess piece that is the most important and able to move in any direction but one square at a time
13 - chess terms.queen: the most powerful piece in the game of chess that can move in any direction
13 - chess terms.rook: a chess piece that is represented by a small tower-shaped object, typically with a pointed top, and is one of the six types of pieces used in the game
13 - chess terms.bishop: a chess piece that is placed next to the king and next to the queen and moves in any direction diagonally
13 - chess terms.knight: a chess piece that looks like the head of a horse and can either move two vertical and one horizontal squares or two horizontal and one vertical squares in any direction
13 - chess terms.pawn: one of the eight weakest pieces in chess, usually smaller in size compared to other pieces
13 - chess terms.black: one of the two opposing players, who moves second and uses pieces that are distinguished by their black color
13 - chess terms.white: one of the two opposing players, who moves first and uses pieces that are distinguished by their white color
13 - chess terms.checkmate: a chess move that makes the opponent's king unable to escape, which means that opponent has lost
13 - chess terms.draw: when neither player is able to win the game, typically because there are no more legal moves available or because both players agree to a draw
13 - chess terms.stalemate: a situation in the game of chess where one is unable to make any legal moves while their king is not checkmated, therefore the game ends and no one wins
13 - chess terms.threefold repetition: a rule that occurs when the same position on the board occurs three times with the same player to move, or if the same sequence of moves occurs three times with the same player to move, resulting in a draw or stalemate
13 - chess terms.time control: the amount of time each player has to make their moves during a game, with various formats and time limits available, such as a fixed amount of time per move or a total time for the entire game, and with additional time increments or time delays added after each move
13 - chess terms.fifty-move rule: a rule in chess stating that if no capture has been made and no pawn has been moved in the previous fifty moves by each player, either player can claim a draw
13 - chess terms.chess set: a collection of pieces used to play the game of chess, typically consisting of 32 pieces in total, with 16 pieces for each player
13 - chess terms.castling: a move in the game of chess that allows the king and one of the rooks to move simultaneously
13 - chess terms.en passant: a special pawn capture move in chess that can occur when a pawn moves two squares forward from its starting position and lands adjacent to an opposing pawn on the fifth rank
13 - chess terms.zugzwang: a term in chess used to describe a situation where a player would prefer to pass their turn and make no move, as any move they can make would put them in a weaker position or lead to an eventual loss
13 - chess terms.check: a chess move that puts the opponent's king under the threat of a direct attack by the chess pieces of the other player
13 - chess terms.chess clock: a device used to time the moves of players during a game of chess, with two clocks typically used for each player, one with a button that stops their clock and starts their opponent's clock, and vice versa
13 - chess terms.fast chess: a type of chess game with a significantly reduced time control compared to traditional chess, typically with each player having only a few minutes or seconds to make their moves
13 - chess terms.algebraic notation: a standardized system used to record and describe the moves made in a game of chess, with each square of the chessboard being assigned a unique letter and number coordinate, and each piece being represented by its first letter
13 - chess terms.scholar's mate: a four-move checkmate sequence in chess that can occur when one player moves their pawn to e4, their bishop to c4, and their queen to h5, threatening to checkmate the opposing king on f7
13 - chess terms.grandmaster: the highest title a player can achieve, awarded by fide to players who have demonstrated exceptional skill and achievement in chess tournaments and matches
13 - chess terms.opening: the initial stage of the game, where players make their first moves to develop their pieces and control the center of the board
13 - chess terms.middlegame: the phase of the game that follows the opening, where players have developed their pieces and are looking to create an advantageous position on the board
13 - chess terms.endgame: the final phase of the game that follows the middlegame, where only a few pieces remain on the board and where the focus shifts to pawn promotion, checkmate, and strategic play with the remaining pieces
13 - chess terms.chess problem: a puzzle or challenge in the game of chess that involves finding a specific sequence of moves that leads to a particular outcome, such as a checkmate or a draw
13 - chess terms.bye: a situation where a player is given a free point without having to play a game, typically due to an odd number of players in the tournament or an uneven number of rounds
13 - chess terms.blunder: a serious tactical or positional mistake that results in a significant disadvantage or loss of material, often leading to a loss of the game
13 - chess terms.combination: a sequence of moves that involves a tactical sacrifice or exchange of material to gain a positional or tactical advantage, often leading to a decisive advantage or checkmate
13 - chess terms.desperado: a piece that is sacrificed with the aim of achieving tactical gains, especially in a losing or desperate situation
13 - chess terms.exchange: the capture of a rook for a minor piece, such as a knight or bishop, or vice versa
13 - chess terms.fool's mate: a two-move checkmate sequence in chess that can occur when one player makes an early mistake by moving their f-pawn or g-pawn too far forward, leaving their king vulnerable to attack
13 - chess terms.fork: a tactic in which a single piece attacks two or more of the opponent's pieces at the same time, forcing the opponent to choose which piece to defend and allowing the attacker to capture the other
13 - chess terms.gambit: (chess) an opening strategy in which a player voluntarily sacrifices a pawn or sometimes a more valuable piece, typically in the early moves of the game
13 - chess terms.open game: a game that features early pawn exchanges and a relatively open center of the board, often resulting in more active and tactical play
13 - chess terms.outpost: a square on the board that is under the control of one player's pawn and cannot be attacked by the opponent's pawns, making it an ideal position for a knight or bishop to occupy and control important squares on the board
13 - chess terms.knight's tour: a mathematical problem and a chess puzzle that involves finding a sequence of moves for a knight that visits every square on an empty chessboard exactly once
13 - chess terms.round-robin: a type of tournament in which each player or team competes against every other player or team in the tournament once. in a round-robin tournament, participants are organized into a single group and play a series of matches, with points being awarded for wins, draws, and losses
13 - chess terms.sacrifice: a deliberate move in which a player gives up material, such as a pawn, knight, bishop, rook, or even a queen, in exchange for a strategic or tactical advantage
13 - chess terms.semi-open game: a chess game that starts with 1.e4, but where black responds with a move other than 1...e5, often resulting in a closed or semi-closed position
13 - chess terms.simultaneous exhibition: a chess event in which a strong player, usually a grandmaster, plays multiple games at the same time against a group of opponents, moving from board to board and making one move at a time
13 - chess terms.double check: a situation where the opponent's king is attacked by two pieces simultaneously, and the king must move because it cannot be protected by capturing one of the attacking pieces
13 - chess terms.discovered check: a tactic where a player moves one of their pieces, revealing an attack on the opponent's king by another piece that was previously blocked or hidden behind the moving piece
13 - chess terms.discovered attack: a tactic where moving one piece uncovers an attack by another piece, creating a double threat and putting pressure on the opponent
13 - chess terms.king's indian defense: a chess opening where black sets up a strong defense and plans to attack the opponent's position later in the game
13 - chess terms.attack: a player's action of threatening to capture an opponent's piece, control key squares, or put the opponent's king in checkmate
13 - chess terms.perpetual check: a situation where one player continuously checks the opponent's king with no possibility of reaching a checkmate, resulting in a drawn game due to a stalemate or a threefold repetition
13 - chess terms.dead draw: a position where neither player has a realistic chance of winning, typically due to a lack of material or a highly symmetrical and locked position, resulting in an inevitable draw if the players continue to play perfectly
13 - chess terms.decoy: a tactical maneuver where a piece is sacrificed or placed in a vulnerable position to lure the opponent into making a disadvantageous move or to redirect their attention away from a more critical part of the board
13 - chess terms.tournament: a series of sporting games in which teams or players compete against different rivals in different rounds until only one remains and that is the winner
13 - chess terms.cross-check: a tactical move in response to a check, where the checked player delivers a counter-check by moving another piece, creating a double threat that must be addressed by the opponent
13 - chess terms.candidate move: a potential move that a player considers during their turn as they analyze the possible outcomes and select the best course of action
13 - chess terms.boden's mate: a rare but elegant checkmate pattern named after samuel boden, where a knight and a bishop coordinate to deliver checkmate to the opponent's king
13 - chess terms.touch-move rule: a fundamental rule in chess that requires a player, who touches one of their own pieces, to move that piece if it has a legal move available
13 - chess terms.tempo: a player's move that gains a move or a tempo over their opponent
13 - chess terms.backward pawn: a pawn that is behind its adjacent pawns on the same file and cannot be easily advanced, making it vulnerable to attacks and potentially weakening the player's pawn structure
13 - chess terms.battery: a setup where two or more pieces of the same color are aligned along a file, rank, or diagonal, increasing their combined attacking power and potential threats to the opponent's position
13 - chess terms.back-rank mate: a checkmate pattern where the opponent's king is trapped on the back rank of the board and is mated by a rook or queen that delivers the checkmate along the same rank
13 - chess terms.bare king: a situation where one player has no pieces left on the board, and their king is the only remaining piece
13 - chess terms.promotion: the rule that allows a pawn to be promoted to a higher-ranking piece when it reaches the opposite end of the board
13 - chess terms.alekhine's gun: a tactical formation where two rooks are stacked on the same file, and the queen is behind them, creating a powerful attacking position
13 - chess terms.pin: a tactical maneuver where a piece is attacked and unable to move without exposing a more valuable piece behind it to capture
13 - chess terms.absolute pin: a pin where the pinned piece is the king, meaning it cannot move without putting the king in check, making it illegal to move the pinned piece
13 - chess terms.international chess federation: the international organization that governs the rules and regulations of chess, as well as organizes and regulates international chess competitions

14 - types of video games.hero shooter: a type of multiplayer video game where players control distinct characters, each with unique abilities or skills, and compete in team-based battles

14 - types of video games.online game: a video game played over the internet on devices such as pcs, gaming consoles, and mobile devices
14 - types of video games.single-player video game: a game played alone, without other people, focusing on individual progress and enjoyment
14 - types of video games.racing game: a type of video game that focuses on players controlling vehicles, such as cars or motorcycles
14 - types of video games.sandbox game: a type of video game that allows players significant freedom and open-world exploration, often featuring nonlinear gameplay and interactive environments where players can shape the game world and create their own experiences

14 - types of video games.sport video game: a genre that simulates real-world sports and allows players to compete in virtual versions of various sports activities
14 - types of video games.strategy video game: a genre that involves planning and decision-making to achieve specific objectives, often in a simulated environment with multiple variables and challenges
14 - types of video games.third-person shooter: a video game genre where the player's character is visible on the screen, and the gameplay primarily involves shooting at enemies from a third-person perspective

15 - role-playing game terms.live-action role play: a form of interactive role-playing game where participants physically act out their characters and engage in a shared narrative within a real-world setting, often with minimal or no use of dice or other game mechanics
15 - role-playing game terms.tabletop role-playing game: a type of game where players assume the roles of fictional characters and collaboratively create a story and adventure, guided by rules and a gamemaster, using dice rolls and imagination to resolve actions and outcomes
15 - role-playing game terms.campaign setting: a fictional or pre-designed world, universe, or environment created for use in tabletop role-playing games, providing a backdrop and context for the game's narrative and adventures
15 - role-playing game terms.threefold model: a theoretical framework used in tabletop role-playing games to classify player preferences and game styles into three main categories: exploration, interaction, and combat
15 - role-playing game terms.gamemaster: the person who runs and oversees a tabletop role-playing game, guiding the players through the game's story and acting as the referee
15 - role-playing game terms.armor class: a numerical representation in tabletop role-playing games, particularly dungeons & dragons, that indicates how difficult it is for a character to be hit or damaged in combat, with higher values making it more challenging for attacks to succeed
15 - role-playing game terms.character sheet: a document, whether physical or digital, used in role-playing games to record and organize the details and statistics of a player's character, including attributes, abilities, skills, and equipment, serving as a reference and resource during gameplay
15 - role-playing game terms.metagaming: the act of using external knowledge or information that is outside the game world to influence in-game decisions, often breaking the immersion and fairness of the game
15 - role-playing game terms.saving throw: a roll of dice in tabletop role-playing games, like dungeons & dragons, made by a player character to resist or mitigate the effects of certain hazards, spells, or other adverse situations
15 - role-playing game terms.game mechanic: a rule or interaction that governs how players interact with the game world and achieve objectives during gameplay
15 - role-playing game terms.troupe system: a role-playing game structure where players collectively control multiple characters, allowing them to rotate and play different roles during the game's narrative and scenes
15 - role-playing game terms.attribute: a specific characteristic or statistic that represents a particular aspect of a character or entity in a game, influencing their abilities and interactions within the game's mechanics and systems
15 - role-playing game terms.party: a group of people who are involved in an activity together for entertainment
15 - role-playing game terms.hit point: a numerical value representing the amount of health or vitality a character or object has in a game or other entertainment medium
15 - role-playing game terms.health: a numerical measure of a character's well-being, typically represented by hit points or life points
15 - role-playing game terms.actual play: recordings, live streams, or sessions where players engage in gameplay, whether in tabletop role-playing games or video games, providing an opportunity for others to observe and experience the game in action
15 - role-playing game terms.gamist-narrativist-simulationist theory: a framework used to classify player preferences in tabletop role-playing games, categorizing them into gamism, narrativism, or simulationism based on their focus on challenge, storytelling, or immersion, respectively
15 - role-playing game terms.campaign: a series of connected missions, quests, or adventures designed to form a cohesive narrative or storyline for players to experience and progress through

16 - video game terms.achievement: a reward in some video games that is obtained after completing specific, often challenging tasks
16 - video game terms.avatar: an image that is the representation of a player in a game or an account on social media
